description: Standing orders with an amount of 2802 or more are used in the per-purpose averages and in the overall average.

a.request: Considering only standing orders (the `order` table) whose `amount` is at least 2802, compute the average `amount` for each payment purpose code (`k_symbol`), treating the blank purpose code as a group of its own. Then take the simple average of those per-purpose averages. Which purposes have an average above that overall figure? For each, list the `k_symbol`, its average amount, and how far it exceeds the overall figure (purpose average minus overall figure), without rounding.
a.sql: WITH big AS (SELECT TRIM(COALESCE(k_symbol, '')) AS purpose, amount FROM `order` WHERE amount >= 2802), purpose_avg AS (SELECT purpose, AVG(amount) AS avg_amount FROM big GROUP BY purpose), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_amount) AS overall_avg FROM purpose_avg) SELECT p.purpose AS k_symbol, p.avg_amount AS avg_amount, p.avg_amount - o.overall_avg AS excess_over_overall FROM purpose_avg p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.avg_amount > o.overall_avg ORDER BY excess_over_overall DESC;

b.request: Which purposes (k_symbol, including the blank code as its own group) have an average order amount, over orders with amount ≥ 2802, that is above the simple mean of those per-purpose averages, and by how much each exceeds it?
b.sql:
WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(k_symbol, '') AS k_symbol, amount
  FROM `order`
  WHERE amount >= 2802
),
per_purpose AS (
  SELECT k_symbol, AVG(amount) AS avg_amount
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY k_symbol
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_amount) AS mean_of_avgs FROM per_purpose
)
SELECT p.k_symbol,
       p.avg_amount,
       p.avg_amount - o.mean_of_avgs AS excess_over_mean
FROM per_purpose p
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE p.avg_amount > o.mean_of_avgs
ORDER BY excess_over_mean DESC;
b.raw: Which purposes (k_symbol, including the blank code as its own group) have an average order amount, over orders with amount ≥ 2802, that is above the simple mean of those per-purpose averages, and by how much each exceeds it?

d.request: Among standing orders with `amount >= 2802` in the `order` table, compute each `k_symbol` group's mean `amount` (with blank `k_symbol` as its own group), take the unweighted mean of those group means as the overall figure, and list each group whose mean exceeds that figure, with its mean and (group mean − overall figure) unrounded.
d.sql: WITH filtered AS (SELECT TRIM(COALESCE(k_symbol, '')) AS k, amount FROM `order` WHERE amount >= 2802), group_means AS (SELECT k, AVG(amount) AS mean_amount FROM filtered GROUP BY k), overall AS (SELECT AVG(mean_amount) AS overall_mean FROM group_means) SELECT g.k AS k_symbol, g.mean_amount AS mean_amount, g.mean_amount - o.overall_mean AS diff_from_overall FROM group_means g CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE g.mean_amount > o.overall_mean;

c.request: Using an `amount` of 2802 as the cutoff for a large standing order (the `order` table), compute the average `amount` of the large orders for each payment purpose code (`k_symbol`), treating the blank purpose code as a group of its own. Then take the simple average of those per-purpose averages. Which purposes have an average above that overall figure? For each, list the `k_symbol`, its average amount, and how far it exceeds the overall figure (purpose average minus overall figure), without rounding. Standing orders with an amount of 2802 or more are used in the per-purpose averages and in the overall average.
c.sql: WITH large AS (SELECT TRIM(k_symbol) AS k_symbol, amount FROM `order` WHERE amount >= 2802), per_purpose AS (SELECT k_symbol, AVG(amount) AS avg_amount FROM large GROUP BY k_symbol), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_amount) AS overall_avg FROM per_purpose) SELECT p.k_symbol, p.avg_amount, p.avg_amount - o.overall_avg AS excess FROM per_purpose p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.avg_amount > o.overall_avg;
